items.s: WALKING Walking section overview of the winter: team wins in the G.L.C. and National Junior, the aim of retaining the McSweeney Trophy, Paul Blagg's form, Richard Dorman's National Junior win and news of Allan Callow and Doug Fothingham. WALKING Except for the Chippenham we failed to win an 'Open' this winter, but were always placed. The reasons we did not pull off a win were through our inability to turn out a full team due to illness, injury and work difficulties and not through non-appearance. In the G.L.C. we did at last all get together and won comfortably from Surrey W.C. Our other main win was of course the National Junior at Coventry, fortunately we had three able to turn out. This year we shall attempt to retain the McSweeney Trophy, but to do this we must produce good performances in the Senior Championships, including the 100 km. to be held this year at Stoke Mandeville, and then hold on to the Under 20s. Paul Blagg has been the star of the winter for us, with Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton often on the side lines. He has produced some excellent performances including 71.26 in the G.L.C. for 2nd and winning the Met.Police 10m Championship in 72.15. With these sort of times one can anticipate some promising long distances from him this year. Richard Dorman produced a stimulating performance to win the National Junior at Coventry in a championship best performance. News of world traveller Allan Callow, he has now taken up full time residence back in his native Isle of Man and reverted back to Boundary Harriers, but still retains 2nd claim to Belgrave. Congratulations to Doug Fothingham for his performance in winning his age group in the Worlds Vets Championship in New Zealand. Walking Reports by .................. items.sum: Report of the 1980 Chippenham to Calne 6 miles walk, where Steve Barry broke Ken Matthews' 1962 course record and Belgrave, led by Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton, won the team prize.
items.s: OCTOBER 11TH 1980 - CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE - 6 MILES Report of the 1980 Chippenham to Calne 6 miles walk, where Steve Barry broke Ken Matthews' 1962 course record and Belgrave, led by Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton, won the team prize. OCTOBER 11TH 1980 - CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE - 6 MILES Saturday afternoon in Chippenham is a busy time with shoppers plus a continuous stream of vehicles. In addition the annual Chippenham to Calne walk contributes 144 walkers plus officials. Shortly before 3 p.m. a policeman halts the traffic and the lady competitors line up and are sent on their way by the Mayor. They are soon followed by 130 men and the 1980 race is under way. Soon in the car to transport timekeepers to Calne we get caught in the traffic hold up. Eventually we catch the tail enders and we are not travelling at the speed of the 8 m.p.h. leaders. A left hand turn takes us away from the A4 and the walkers and eventually back on the course but now ahead of the field. The finish on the Green at Calne where the Mayor awaits has separate funnels for men and women. Soon the warning cry arises "here he comes" and looking at the watches the time is just under 41 minutes as the leader reaches the top of the Green and Steve Barry (Roath) competes the final distance to the finish to break the course record set by Ken Matthews in 1962 of 42m 47s by no less than 1m 25s. The wind was favourable but certainly not to the extent of the margin by which the record was broken, and so the new record holder wins the Gold Medal which has been waiting since Ken Matthews record was made. Next, only 9 seconds outside the old record, came Richard Dorman and 8 seconds behind Carl Lawton, superb walking by our two. Mike Scamell and John Newnham are soon in and our hopes of retaining the team title look good, Steve Marshall, Mike Nicholls and Edie Crossingham are next home all under 50 mins. and then Martin Hills and Joe Scamell. On to the prize giving at the fine sports centre where once again we collect the team prize which include the monster pie. Richard also wins the 1st Junior award (his time was 3rd fastest ever). The Handicapper managed to spread the 10 prizes amongst 9 Clubs with Steve Marshall taking one. We drew blanks in the raffle but we must not grumble and maybe just as well judging by Carl's well laden van, trophies, grub and competitors etc. Yet again another well organised event and of course Jack and Joan Goswell were in on producing the results. items.h: NOVEMBER 22ND 1980 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN 7 / THE BERMAN CUP
items.sum: Report and results of the club's 61st Open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon on 22 November 1980, with the history of the Berman Cup and of chief judge Joe Coleman; Leicester W.C. beat Belgrave for the team prize.
items.s: NOVEMBER 22ND 1980 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN 7 / THE BERMAN CUP Report and results of the club's 61st Open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon on 22 November 1980, with the history of the Berman Cup and of chief judge Joe Coleman; Leicester W.C. beat Belgrave for the team prize. NOVEMBER 22ND 1980 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN 7 THE BERMAN CUP Most of our Club Trophies are named after their donors mostly prominent Belgravians of the past. The 'Berman Cup' is awarded by the Club. Originally it was competed for in the Open '7s' in the thirties being allocated to a different event each year. This mattered little as our team led by the late Harry Churcher used to make a clean sweep of the Opens and by winning it for three consecutive years it became our trophy and nowadays it goes to the team which wins our own Open 7 miles Walk. The 61st 'Open' was held on 22nd November and good weather prevailed. Our President, Carl Lawton started the race which had the usual array of Club Officials, Chief Judge was Joe Coleman who himself was a regular member of our winning teams. He was third in the A.A.A. 7 Miles Championship in 1938 and in 1939, also in 1939 he was awarded the Fowler Dixon Style prize. Many remember his dead heat with his brother Len in the R.W.A. 'Junior' Championship in 1938. Amongst the judges were George Bentley, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Sid Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson and refereeing was Ray Hall. Again the course was changed using three laps of the hills using a less steep hill than previous. New Zealander Mike Parker (Brighton) and D. Jarman (S.W.C.) were soon clear of the field and as the race progressed the further ahead they were and at the finish we had to wait nearly 2½ minutes before the third man arrived. Our first man in was John Hall (7th) with John Newnham doing well for 12th. We can perhaps note that not only were we without Carl but Richard Dorman, Paul Blagg and Mike Scamell were non-starters. Nevertheless Mike Nicholls and Steve Marshall (16th & 17th) came through well to complete the team. We were the first club to finish four, but our Midland rivals, Leicester W.C. soon had their fourth man in to give them a three point victory. With eight handicap prizes to compete for, our other walkers had plenty to go for and the ever consistent Doug Fotheringham was rewarded with 2nd place, Steve Marshall 4th and John Dunsford (with Doug preparing for their trip to New Zealand) 8th. With the addition of John Hall we also won handicap team. The London Business Houses Championship was held in conjunction and John Hall (Civil Service) and John Dunsford (Lon.Transport D.L.) were 3rd and 5th. An all Belgrave team John Hall, Bromley and Keown were second team. Once again, Jack and Joan Goswell produced their immaculate result sheet which showed 110 starters and 15 teams. Finally our thanks to Carl under whose guidance the race went without a hitch. items.s: MARCH 7th 1981 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA 10M / SOUTHERN CHAMPIONS AGAIN Report and placings of the S.A.R.W.A. Southern 10 miles walking championship at Battersea Park on 7 March 1981, where Belgrave retained the team title without Paul Blagg and John Hall. MARCH 7th 1981 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA 10M SOUTHERN CHAMPIONS AGAIN The S.A.R.W.A. held their Championship Meeting at Battersea Park on March 7th, the main event being the Ten Miles Senior Championship, preceded by a Ladies 5 Kilos. We had no representatives in the first race - a situation we hope will soon be put right. By the time the Ten Miles started it was raining and unfortunately, we were without Paul Blagg, whose accident is reported elsewhere, John Hall too was an absentee. Nevertheless, we had quite a good line-up to defend the title we won last year over the same course, basically five laps of the road round the Park. After the first lap we emerged from our shelter under a tree to see that Carl and Richard (who won the Individual title last year) were going well in about sixth position, later came Edie and Mike, also together, and a good team placing was in the making. Others were banging away over the familiar circuit. As the laps went by our positions were consolidated and with a lap to go, Carl was fourth, moving in top gear and we weren't surprised when he had picked up a place to finish third. Richard, getting back to form soon came in and it was good to see Edie maintaining his recent good form with a powerful and stylish finish, to be followed soon by the consistent Mike to give us a team win again. Happily the rain eased off over the last stages. As usual we had good performances from our others, our Vets, led by World Champion Doug Fotheringham with John Bromley and Joe Scammell would surely have beaten any other Clubs trio. With so many walkers "barred" we couldn't field a team in the Garnet Cup, held in conjunction. 1.I.McCombie (Camb.H) 72.00; 2.R.Bestley (Ton) 74.05; 3.C.Lawton 74.56; 5.R.Dorman 76.42; 11. items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1980-81 cross-country winter, with results from the Surrey Womens Road Relays, the Surrey Womens Cross Country League and the ladies' club championships, and a look ahead to the track season. WITH THE LADIES Only a few results. Not many of our ladies seem to be interested in cross-country. However, a small group (the faithful few) started going over the country on Saturday afternoons. Our first meeting was the Surrey Womens Road Relays at Brockwell Park on a sunny but very windy day. We were also entered in the Surrey Womens Cross Country League which consisted of 4 matches for three age groups - Girls, Juniors and Seniors. 15 Clubs had entered for this league and the first of the matches was our own promotion on Wimbledon Common. The 3 races provided a total of 197 finishers with 100 in the girls race. I would like to take this opportunity of thanking all of those who came along to help at Wimbledon. Unfortunately we did not contest the last two fixtures in this League due to injury, illness, unavailability. I would like to thank Cross Country Captain Joanne Warnett (leader of the faithful few) for her efforts in trying to get teams out. She has worked extremely hard in trying to encourage people to go over the country and also ran at Wimbledon despite not feeling very well. Finally, I would like to say thank you to Ray Hall for all his efforts this winter. We were all pleased to see him back with us again. items.s: STRANGER THAN FICTION! Humorous anecdote of an exchange between John Bicourt and Surrey veterans' champion Pat O'Connor on a training run over Wimbledon Common. STRANGER THAN FICTION! John Bicourt, training over Wimbledon Common on one of those weekends when he was not running elsewhere, encouraged Surrey Vet Champ. Pat O'Connor to go out for a steady 10 mile spin. The reported conversation from a usually reliable source went as follows at about the 6 mile mark: Pat. Dis is a bit fast John. Are all yor runs loik dis? John No Pat; bit faster on my own. Pat Den oim glad I dont trains wid ya when yor on ya own!! (collapse of pack.) John Bicourt John Bicourt John Bicourt John Pat O'Connor Pat O'Connor Surrey veterans' champion Pat O'Connor Pat Pat. Wimbledon Common

items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Bill Laws's introduction to the youths' winter reports, on illness and injury among the younger athletes and their overall good season. YOUNG ATHLETES Like many football clubs struggling for promotion the Xmas period often determines how events will turn out in the Spring. Of our younger athletes Dave North was sidelined before the New Year due to illness but has produced a remarkable come-back since. On the other hand Mark Waller has lost some fitness recently due to school studies, injury and jet setting. John Gladwin has had very bad luck since February. Having beaten Ledger of AFD into 3rd place in the Surrey Junior C.C. he then had to stand by through flu and leg injury to watch ledger finish 5th in the Junior Inter-Counties and 8th in the Junior National. We wish John luck in his battle to shake off injury. Stuart Paton has also improved since Christmas following flu and German Measles. The following reports confirm that overall it has been a good winter with excellent performances all round and although some patchiness due to illness and injury has resulted it is very pleasing to see our younger members still together, still enthusiastic and still improving. Well done, keep it going! NOVEMBER 22nd 1980 - GATESHEAD - SCHWEPPES INTERNATIONAL C.C. Two of our younger and very mobile members travelled to Gateshead to run in supporting races at the Schweppes International Cross County Championships. Both acquited themselves well. Stuart Paton finished 68th in the Senior open race and was well pleased to beat 5 of Scotlands Junior C.C. Team (he hopes to make it this year) and Paul Richley finished a fine 30th place in the Youths event. items.s: Championship Double Report and results of the Surrey cross-country championships at Happy Valley, Coulsdon, on 3 January 1981, where Paul Richley retained the youths' title for Belgrave (printed P.Ritchley in the results), John Gladwin took junior silver behind C. Hensby and Belgrave won the Surrey junior team title for the first time since 1963. Championship Double JANUARY 3rd 1981 - HAPPY VALLEY COULSDON - SURREY C.C. CHAMPS. Following last years successes in winning both the individual and team Surrey Youth's titles it was expected that this years races would be something of an anti-climax. Gerry Sexton who had finished 6th in 1980 as a first year Youth had experienced bad luck through injury and illness while the transition to Junior ranks was expected to prove too much for the rest of last years winning Youths team. Add to that the last minute withdrawal of Stuart Paton with 'flu and even the most optimistic supporter would have given odds against a medal of any colour. How different it was on the day. Our Colts finished a team for the first time in many years. Michael Blackmore ran a very creditable 18th in the boys race and then Paul Richley pulled out all the stops to win the Youths title having followed every attempt by the talented Andy Leyland to drop him around the hilly course. In the event it was Paul who broke away up the last hill and coasted home to retain for Belgrave the title which Dave north had won last year. The revelation in the Junior race was John Gladwin who is now showing tremendous stamina to add to his blistering track speed. With the leading group from the start John held on to Hensby and Ledger until the half-way mark when Hensby made a distained break. Soon after pre-race favourite Ledger found John too hot to handle and it was an individual Silver for the Belgravian - a remarkable and possibly unique feat by a first year Surrey Junior. It was the team result, however, which took everyone by surprise. Woking closed 3 men in 10 but had to wait till the 40's for their 4th man. In the meantime a best ever run by Junior Captain Mark Waller ably backed by Dave North (on only 30 miles training) and Mark Sinclair ensured a surprise victory for our team. A quick check confirmed that this was our first Surrey Junior team title since 1963. Congratulations to all our youngsters. items.s: FEBRUARY 14th 1981 - TRENT PARK - SOUTHERN C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and Belgrave results from the Southern cross-country championships at Trent Park, where the juniors finished ninth as a team; youths' results were not sent to the editor. FEBRUARY 14th 1981 - TRENT PARK - SOUTHERN C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Traditionally our young athletes peak for the Surreys and so we do not expect too much in the National and Southerns. It was good to see Stuart Paton coming back to fitness in the Junior team as well as the rapid and indeed remarkable improvement by Dave North after only 1 months solid work following an illness which prevented training for the second half of 1980. Mark Waller ran a steady race while it was pleasing to see John Searle, up from Kent University, bringing the team home in a creditable 9th place. Mark Sinclair ran below form and is currently going through a bad patch which we know he will overcome with determination. In the Youths race Paul Richley was a bit below form and such is the high standard that 30 seconds down can mean 30 lost places. Gerry Sexton continued his fight for form. 1.I.Stewart (Inv) 31.04; 2.G.Wightman (Dart) 31.14; 3.M.Lassater (Brighton) 31.37. items.s: 'SOUPER' RECORD Light-hearted note on Paul Richley's free-soup record at the Southern and National cross-country championships. 'SOUPER' RECORD A feature at several of this years major C.C. races has been the appearance of a gaudy red Range Rover and caravan manned by an enthusiastic crew of uniformed ladies providing free soup for competitors and spectators. After the Southern Champs we lost sight of Paul Richley and later discovered that, using a variety of disguises, he had managed to down four helpings. Imagine his delight on seeing the same outfit after the Nationals. The record now stands at six helpings and even Paul admitted that he was filling up. Now we know his training secrets! DOUBLE WIN NOVEMBER 8th 1980 - COULSDON - SURREY VETS C.C. CHAMPS. Pat O'Connor and Charlie Walker brought home the claret and gold in first place in the over 40 and over 50 age groups respectively in the Surrey Championships held over a testing Coulsdon course. Charlie Walker caught the attention of the Athletic Press who remembered that it was precisely 30 years ago that he won the senior title. Charlie is so enthusiastic about his running that the intervening period has involved a constant barrage of anecdotes from this enthusiastic man. Second in the chat stakes is Pat O'Connor who can beat Patrick Moore at the quick talk business when he puts his mind to it. Sadly the back-up support was lacking. MARCH 15th 1981 - CRYSTAL PALACE - CROYDON RELAYS (VETS 5-STAGE) New Vets Section Secretary, Bob Kersey, had less than 1 week from taking on the job to pull together a team for the Croydon Relays. With Laurie O'Hara working, and Pat O'Connor plus Brian Gorman, Trevor Hart and Lionel Mann running the previous day in the Club 5¾ it seemed unlikely that we could get a team together. Bob's persuasive powers prevailed and the result was 2nd team with Keith Sinclair turning in one of his best runs to be fastest vet of the day. Keith's keeness is legendary. Instead of drinking his Sherry prize he used it as leg embrocation prior to an evening training spin. There's dedication for you Blodwin! Teams: 1.Epsom & E. 5909. 2.Belgrave 60.59. items.label: April 1981
items.sum: Review of the senior men's winter season: relegation from Division I of the Surrey League despite the talent available, with bright spots in the young runners, newcomer Graham Macky, full teams in the National and 17th in the Haig Southern 12-stage relay.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY Review of the senior men's winter season: relegation from Division I of the Surrey League despite the talent available, with bright spots in the young runners, newcomer Graham Macky, full teams in the National and 17th in the Haig Southern 12-stage relay. ROAD AND COUNTRY We entered the winter period with the pleasant prospect of an improvement in our fortunes. Sure enough the better of our middle distance runners were getting a bit long in the tooth but nonetheless we expected some solid performances as usual. Add to this our talented batch of up and coming junior athletes and our stay in Division I of the North Surrey League seemed assured. In the event it turned out badly. The talent was there but in practice we could not get more than half our top best twelve out at any one time. And so from a promising start we slipped to the bottom of the league and are once again relegated. A close perusal of the names of our scoring teams and the relatively close margin of 329 points between 2nd and 7th will show you how easy it should have been to stay up. The bright spots were there. Our younger runners performed exceptionally well (See Young Athletes Section) and out of the blue came a new member - Graham Macky - a very talented and enthusiastic runner from New Zealand, who has revelled in the competition with which we have provided him. A modest but encouraging sign that we are on the road to recovery is that for the first time in many years we completed all teams in the National Cross Country Championships. And finally we got it together with a much improved team effort in our own Haig Southern 12 stage road relay in which we finished 17th . It was pleasing to see Chris Steer qualifying for this race during a three week visit from the U.S.A. Graham Macky Graham Macky new member from New Zealand (slarchive lists a G Mackie) Chris Steer Chris Steer qualified for the Haig relay team during a three-week visit from the U.S.A. Gladwin's Clear Win DECEMBER 13th 1980 - WIMBLEDON - 7½ MILE CLUB C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Before the start of this race we were asked by a passing 'Jogger' if he could join in. The man concerned was Graham Macky out on a 24 mile training spin. He pushed junior John Gladwin to a very fast winning time and gained the scalps of Kortenray and O'Hara. And so this was a day to remember. John gained his first Senior Club Championship and New Zealander Graham Macky joined Belgrave. items.s: Championship / MARCH 14th 1981 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE R.RACE CHAMPIONSHIP Report and full results of the Belgrave 5¾-mile club road championship at Wimbledon, won by Ian Duncan from Graham Macky, with Pete Hardwick winning the handicap. A photo of Macky leading Duncan is on page 30. Championship MARCH 14th 1981 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE R.RACE CHAMPIONSHIP Ian Duncan who has improved remarkably with every race this winter outkicked Graham Macky up Cambridge and maintained a clear lead to the finish. Ian was rewarded with his first Club Road Championship and a personal best time as well. Both Ian and Graham recorded the fastest times for several years. Surrey Youths C.C. Champ. Paul Richley proved how promising he is with a good 30.24 and there were several p.b.'s from other of our improving runners particularly pleasing was Pete Hardwick's breakthrough and he duly won the handicap. Belgrave Relay APRIL 4th 1981 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE/HAIG SOUTHERN 12 STAGE RELAY For the first time in several years Gordon Biscoe was presented with a team selection problem. He had declared that selection depended on 3 races; the 5¾, Cambridge and Cranford Relays. Our potentially fastest short leg runner - John Gladwin was sidelined with injury and with several runners permutating 1 out of 3 and others ignoring the qualifying races completely it was difficult to select the last few places on the available evidence. In the event the first 6 places selected themselves with Graham Mackey handing over 30 seconds off the lead. Junior Stuart Paton ran a blinder and handed over only 4 seconds behind the 5th placed team. John Bicourt and Paul Richley continued to keep hopes high but Ian Duncan failed to repeat his 5¾ form and continues to find this race his bete noir. Chris Steer ran above expectations and Peter Hardwick confirmed that his 5¾ run was no fluke - Welcome to the 'A' team Pete! Laurie and Leo ran well but both admitted that the London Marathon of the previous week must have slowed them. Nonetheless we turned in our best time for 4 years and had Croydon, Blackheath and Brighton behind us. Next year it could well be that many other of our eager youngsters who were taking notes this time will make the team. Teams: 1.A.F.D. 4:06.39; 2.T.V.H. 4:10.39; 3.Invicta 4:12.25; 4.A.F.D. items.label: April 1981
items.sum: Profile by Gordon Doubleday of H.E. (Bert) Footer, the man chiefly responsible for Belgrave's National cross-country wins of 1935, 1939, 1946 and 1948, covering his international and relay career, 1930s pack training, the London to Brighton Relay, the 1939 Poly Marathon and his war service, with a 1930s team photo.
items.s: BERT FOOTER / "IN TERROREM" Profile by Gordon Doubleday of H.E. (Bert) Footer, the man chiefly responsible for Belgrave's National cross-country wins of 1935, 1939, 1946 and 1948, covering his international and relay career, 1930s pack training, the London to Brighton Relay, the 1939 Poly Marathon and his war service, with a 1930s team photo. BERT FOOTER "IN TERROREM" This was the title of an article which appeared in the Belgravian many years ago, its author was H.E. (Bert) Footer, the man chiefly responsible for our wins in the E.C.C.U. Championships (The National) in 1935, 1939, 1946 and 1948. He was trying to urge the lads on to greater efforts. Now 76 years of age he is living in retirement at Ramsgate, we are sorry to say that he suffers from arthritis in both hips and has trouble with his breathing, he has to walk with the aid of sticks. It became his ambition for Belgrave to win the National and in so doing he collected many honours for himself, Surrey Champion, Inter-Counties representative many times, Southern Champion and International finishing fourth at Caerleon in 1933 and fourth again the following year at Ayr. In these two races he was a member of the winning English team, also in the team was Arthur Penny, they both did much to further the good name of the Club. He was also Club Champion and his name can be seen on the Macher and Blackstaffe Shields. So, how in the thirties did he get the rest of the team to such a peak that they could call themselves National Champions? The chief ingredient was training as a pack. If you were in the team, or even if you weren't, he expected you to train with the pack Saturdays at Wimbledon, or on what the Fixture Lists described as "Social Runs" with other clubs. Although not races they seemed to be the next best thing! Other Clubs would join us at Wimbledon or we joined them, the Grandstand at Epsom Downs was a favourite venue with a run out to Walton Heath and back. Midweek it was Tuesdays and Thursdays round Rotten Row (Hyde Park) from the "Rising Sun", Ebury Bridge Road - through Belgravia! On Mondays and Wednesdays you were encouraged to train from home, and Bert and a few others had a tough course in the Southfields - Wimbledon Park area. Friday was rest day, but Sundays - no matter how hard you had gone on Saturdays he and others used to do an all day, stroll over hilly rough country. In case that wasn't enough he had a schedule of home exercises to strengthen the chest, shoulders, abdomen etc. even those who did hard manual work performed their exercises daily. For many years Birchfield Harriers had virtually monopolised the National and in the early thirties Bert's team began to figure in the placings with corresponding performances in the Southern. Not only did we score many wins in the Surrey County Championship but our Middlesex members (running as Cadogan A.C.) would win their County title. We won the Southern in 1934 and in 1935 we travelled to Hall Barn, Beaconsfield for the National, having taken second place to Surrey A.C. in the Southern, held at Hassocks (Sussex). As the runners entered the final lap a quick check up showed us to be in the lead and, shouted on by a coach load of supporters we gained the day and Birchfield's monopoly was ended. It was a proud moment when Bert led the team to collect the winning trophy and their medals. Congratulations to Bert and the Club poured in from all quarters. Our hopes then went forward to the London to Brighton Relay, held a few weeks later. There was no National Road Relay, but whoever won this famous race (promoted by the "News of the World") could regard themselves as Britain's Number One Club in this department. Having won the race in 1934 our Midland rivals were out for revenge! The race from The Houses of Parliament to the front at Brighton consisted of twelve stages of different lengths and of different terrains regarding hills. Not only did you have to have twelve good runners, but you had to put them on the right stages. Here Bert's knowledge of the team enabled him to deploy them to the best advantage, he himself doing the eleventh stage of over five miles from Hickstead to Pyecombe at the top of Dale Hill. Birchfield put up a great fight but Bert was first up Dale Hill to hand over a lead which we maintained to the finish. In 1936, 1937 and 1938 the team trained hard but Birchfield won at Alderley Edge and again at Stratford-on-Avon Racecourse, next year our local rivals, Mitcham A.C. won it back for the South at Reading. However, in 1939 on a muddy course near Manchester we gained our second National win. During the summer Bert took part in and won many road races and figured in our track teams, who regularly won Open Team Races over two and three miles - a feature of the Open Handicap meetings which were very popular. He also competed in the A.A.A. Six Miles Track Championship, and in 1936, was first reserve for G.B. team for the 10,000 metres at the Berlin Olympics. He turned his attention to the Marathon and prepared himself with his usual thoroughness for the 1939 Poly Marathon. Third to arrive at Chiswick Track was a very tired Footer, and the vocal encouragement of Club Supporters helped him over an agonising lap of the track. In September World War II started and he joined the Royal Marine Commandoes - whose tough training must have appealed to him. He was in some tough assignments and when the war ended he resumed his running. The first post-war National, held at Leamington in 1946 saw us win again, but he was not in the scoring team. Next year the Lancs. Club Sutton H. pushed us into second place over a snowbound course at Apsley, (Herts) but next year at Sheffield we won again. After a long distinguished career as a runner, he joined us in 1922, and as cross-country Captain and six years of war he was past his best and retired from the sport. The Club honoured him by electing him an Honorary Life Member and a Vice-President. He was offered the Presidency but was unable to accept. A great pity - our best wishes to you Bert. Gordon Doubleday L to R A.Allum, H.E.Footer, A.E.Taylor, A.R.Shaw, S.Warboys Arthur Penny, J.E.Flower, H.W.Shields, Tom Carter and W.A.Rice H.E. (Bert) Footer H.E. items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and field section introduction noting Ernest Obeng's third Tommy Green Cup, Bill Laws's new Belgrave Masters Coaching Scheme starting at Battersea Park, and Alan Mead's resignation as Sectional Secretary. TRACK AND FIELD Winter is the close season for track and field. However, at the Club Dinner/ Dance summer seemed nearer as Pan African sprint champion Ernest Obeng received the Tommy Green Cup for the third successive year. During the winter, Bill Laws has been hatching a new Coaching Scheme. Supported by finance from both the Sports Council and Wandsworth Borough Council the Belgrave Masters Coaching Scheme as it is to be known, commences at Battersea Park on April 26th at Battersea Park. (See following report). And sadly, as we go to press, we learn that Alan Mead has resigned as Sectional Secretary. Fortunately all the fixtures for the summer have been arranged and Alan has left things in good order. His replacement(s) have not been identified and all track and field members should contact their nearest committee members concerning training, events, appearances etc. During this difficult period we ask all potential competitors to use their initiative and make certain to keep in touch with officials who will be down at Battersea Park track on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays. items.sum: Announcement of the Belgrave Masters Coaching Scheme, funded by the Sports Council and Wandsworth Sports Council, starting at Battersea Park on 26 April 1981 with master coaches Malcolm Coomber, Mike Winch and Ron Wyld.
items.s: NEW COACHING SCHEME / THE BELGRAVE MASTERS COACHING SCHEME Announcement of the Belgrave Masters Coaching Scheme, funded by the Sports Council and Wandsworth Sports Council, starting at Battersea Park on 26 April 1981 with master coaches Malcolm Coomber, Mike Winch and Ron Wyld. NEW COACHING SCHEME THE BELGRAVE MASTERS COACHING SCHEME We have been successful in attracting financial support of £500 from the Sports Council and £150 from the Wandsworth Sports Council to help get the new Belgrave Masters Coaching Scheme off the ground. The scheme will run for 5 months starting on April 26th 1981 and will bring together top coaches and athletes covering all track and field disciplines. A tremendous response from our own club members has enabled a back-up team to be prepared so that coaching will be available on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays throughout the summer. MASTER COACHES The participating Master Coaches are: 1. Malcolm Coomber - Battersea Park - Sprints, Hurdles, Flat Jumps. Malcolm coaches our own Ernest Obeng. Southern Coach. 2. Mike Winch - Battersea Park - Throws. Mike is the UK's No.1 field events athlete and is a National Coach. 3. Ron Wyld - Battersea Park - High Jump. Coaches Ossie Cham. Southern Coach. Also covering middle distance will be our own John Bicourt at Battersea Park and John Sullivan at Wimbledon. Press and School coverage for the scheme has been good and we anticipate a large influx of new talent. It is planned to measure the performance of newcomers at regular intervals on the following days: April 26th May 24th June and July All meetings will start prompt at 10 a.m. on those Sundays. items.sum: Editorial on the coming of sponsorship and financial reward in athletics, the risk of big clubs poaching talent, the club's progress and new committee members, and Haringey's rise as an example to follow before the 1987 centenary.
items.s: TIMES! THEY ARE ACHANGING! Editorial on the coming of sponsorship and financial reward in athletics, the risk of big clubs poaching talent, the club's progress and new committee members, and Haringey's rise as an example to follow before the 1987 centenary. TIMES! THEY ARE ACHANGING! The recent moves towards direct financial reward for top athletes is seen by most people in our sport as an inevitable trend belatedly following the examples of others. It now seems that sponsorship, advertising and all the publicity which goes with these activities will be the lot of those making the big time. It is possible to imagine that even at local level the opportunities to obtain advertising revenue and sponsorship will increase. It is to be hoped that some of the 'new' money will contribute to enhancing grass roots athletics. So far most clubs have existed by many people giving freely of their time and money and the reward has been team spirit, loyalty - in a word - togetherness. The future will bring problems. It will be tempting for larger clubs to hunt for talent carefully developed by smaller clubs. We hope that such practices will not develop, but in case they do it must be our objective to work for a stronger more financially secure club with ever improving facilities. In this issue we record the good progress made on several fronts. In addition we note the number of new Committee members who already are taking an active part in our day to day activities. They are getting the basic experience which we hope will lead to further and deeper involvement in the years ahead. If anyone believes we have a daunting task they're right. But look at Haringay. Seven years ago they started with 15 members. Now they have; excellent facilities, a membership of over 1000, 4 track and field teams and won this year's G.R.E. Gold Cup as well as finishing second in the G.R.E. British League. Not bad going. We now have 5 years until our Centenary. What can we achieve in that period. Its up to all of us! G.R.E. Gold Cup British League Haringay

items.s: grapevine Club news column covering John Bicourt's running and coming baby, Gordon Doubleday's move to Bath, Chris Steer's move to Seattle, Frank Simmons at the AGM, Mrs. Savage's illness and Percy Wright's Esperanto travels. grapevine Elsewhere in this issue we report some first class performances by Stalwart John Bicourt, John has been running fast recently, but not as fast as the stork. We understand that the Bicourts happy event is to be in March and we send our congratulations and best wishes to Val. Gordon Doubleday, who among his many activities is a great contributor to this gazette, has moved from Merton to Bath where he is enjoying his retirement. Gordon still comes up by coach for major events and is in constant touch with Belgrave events. His new address is:- [address withheld]. Chris Steer has moved from San Francisco to Seattle following his return to the U.S.A. after making an impact on our road running teams in the spring. Says the training is better so will we see him again next year? We were delighted to see Frank Simmons at our recent A.G.M. Frank had a few comments on our 'Masters' coaching scheme and hopes to be back at Battersea Park next year where he intends to 'sort' the Ladies Section out. Frank has been seriously ill and has had 2 major abdominal operations, but is progressing well now. Certainly the old sparkle was there. We are sorry to learn that Mrs. Savage has had another spell in hospital and from time to time we hear from Win Shepherd of her progress. A busy time for Win, but it is good that Win. has attended a number of our meetings, helping out, of course. Mrs. Savages' many friends amongst our older members will join in sending their best wishes. Our Honorary Life Member, Percy Wright has for many years (going back to the thirties) been an ardent user of the International Language, Esperanto. He is also a keen caravan tourer and last year he combined these two interests and spent a few weeks touring Europe. This included a visit to the Soviet Union where he met some pen friends, including one in Kiev who took him around Kiev and showed him places of interest. Percy maintains that Esperanto is an easier language to learn than any other. PAST PRESIDENT It is the custom (some say misfortune) for Belgrave President's to retain their official duties during their year of office. For Carl Lawton this was not enough. Not only did he continue to manage the walking section he increased his training to such an extent that he won the London - Brighton Walk this year. What a performance! We now learn that after stepping down Carl is taking on further duties and is looking after membership and subscriptions with his usual enthusiasm and thoroughness. items.sum: Finance report from the A.G.M. showing a £2,269 surplus for the year to June 1981 thanks largely to the bar at Belgrave Hall, followed by a note on the disappointing 100 x 1 mile relay sponsorship, which raised £114.
items.s: MONEY MATTERS Finance report from the A.G.M. showing a £2,269 surplus for the year to June 1981 thanks largely to the bar at Belgrave Hall, followed by a note on the disappointing 100 x 1 mile relay sponsorship, which raised £114. MONEY MATTERS FUND RAISING IMPROVES For those of us who believe a financially strong position is essential to build up all aspects of Club performance in the next few years, one of the A.G.M's main highlights is the report by our Hon.Treasurer, Jim Heathfield. You will recall that 2 years ago we were in the red and last year we reaped the first financial benefits of our new bar and Social Club at Belgrave Hall. This year a combination of increased revenue from subscriptions and the bar and social side have seen a massive upsurge with a "profit" for the year of £2,269. The cost of running the club for the year to June 1981 was a huge £6,407 of which £3,148 was current account expenditure mainly consisting of Printing, Postage etc. (£1,151) and Team and Track fees (£921). Belgrave Hall costs £3,259 to operate and maintain. Income, however, reached a record £8,676. Subscriptions only totalled £2,051 so where did the rest come from? Well, the major contribution of £2,695 came from the bar due to the tremendous work of the team of volunteers who helped out at Socials and the usual weekly events. Next came donations which at £1,421 reflect the support of many members who would like to help but are unable to visit Belgrave Hall regularly. The rest of the income came from all the numerous fund raising activities which are organised throughout the year. So when next we think about the level of subscriptions let us remember that they only contribute 30% towards the costs of running Belgrave. The main income comes from those dedicated members who work so hard to keep "the teams on the road". 100 X 1 MILE SPONSORSHIP The annual 100 x 1 mile relay offers an ideal opportunity for fund raising. We've never really made the most of the chance and this year was no better. No one would take on the responsibility of promoting the sponsorship potential of this event and so all we could do was circulate members asking for their help. Of the 120 requests sent out only 12 members responded. Once again Ross Martin topped the list having raised £30, the second highest being collected by the Richleys who have given tremendous support in one way or another over the last year. The total sum collected was £114. Our thanks to those who helped. If there is anyone who has yet to return monies to Bill Laws, will they please do so as soon as possible. Jim Heathfield Jim Heathfield Hon. DRAW FOOTBALL TICKETS REPLACED BY '200' CLUB The sale of football tickets which for so long have been a major source of revenue has finally ceased and is to be replaced by a new scheme known as the '200' Club. This new enterprise will be headed by Jack Goswell who for so long has looked after the sale of football tickets backed of course by many willing helpers. Details of the '200' Club are sent with this issue of the Belgravian. Briefly, membership is limited to 200 people each paying £1 per month. There is a monthly draw for prizes of £50, £20, £10, and 2 x £5 and twice a year the first prize will be £100. Already 100 people have applied and its the first 200 who can join after which you will have to wait until someone leaves. The first draw is planned to take place in December - so hurry! hurry! items.sum: Profile of the new club president Derek Crookes: his running career since joining in 1954, his illness and comeback, and his many administrative posts in and outside Belgrave.
items.s: President Profile of the new club president Derek Crookes: his running career since joining in 1954, his illness and comeback, and his many administrative posts in and outside Belgrave. President Derek Crookes Derek Crookes joined Belgrave 27 years ago in October 1954 at the age of 14 and he was soon making an impact, winning our Youths C.C. Championship. His athletics career continued to blossom and he holds the unusual distinction of having won both our Junior 100m and 1 mile Championships. His interest in athletics ran parallel to his academic studies and he moved to London University where he gained a full 'purple' and an Honours Degree in Mathematics. During this period he achieved 4.22.0 for the mile and 1.59.0 for the 880 yds. The then current vogue for long distance events also appealed and Derek was soon training for his first marathon - The Poly - and in 1963 he turned in a respectable 2.42.0. This was to be his last major race for 16 years because in 1963 he became seriously ill and needed major surgery - the recovery from which was a slow, protracted business. There seemed little chance of running again but Derek did come back and in 1979 managed to make our Southern 12 stage relay team. Although unable to train and compete as he would have liked, Derek has become involved in many official duties both within and outside Belgrave. From 1964-1967 he was Road Running Secretary during a period when our Senior teams were the scourge of the South. He has organised our 20 Mile race for the last 8 years. In 1977 he took on the onerous post of Club Secretary, which position he still holds. Outside Belgrave he has enhanced our reputation by serving on several Committees. He has been Assistant Secretary to the SCAAA for the past 5 years, South of Thames Secretary for 6 years and has served on the Surrey County AAA's Committee for 3 years. Derek's continuing hard work on behalf of Belgrave would not be possible without the support of his wife Mary who is frequently to be seen, helping out at various social functions. To undertake a year of Presidential responsibilities and still maintain a formidable list of official posts would be a daunting task for all, but the strongest and determined of characters. We are indeed fortunate that Derek is such a person and with the support of his family and fellow Belgravians we can expect that this year will continue to see the improvement in our fortunes. Derek Crookes Derek Crookes President 1981; joined October 1954 aged 14; won club Youths C.C., Junior 100m and 1 mile championships; 4.22.0 mile, 1.59.0 880 yds, 2.42.0 Poly marathon 1963; Road Running Secretary 1964-67; Club Secretary from 1977; organiser of the club 20 Mile race; SCAAA Assistant Secretary, South of Thames Secretary Derek Crookes Derek Mary Crookes Mary Derek Crookes's wife Polytechnic Marathon Southern 12 Stage Road Relay Belgrave 20 Mile race Club Championships London University SCAAA South of Thames Surrey County AAA

From The President I would like to say what a great honour it is to have been elected President (the 50th by my calculations) of Belgrave. I intend to be present at as many club fixtures as possible and sincerely hope all active athletes - especially those of 'A' team standard - will make this the year of the fixture card. That is, turning out for the established races such as the Surrey League, in which we hope for promotion back to Div.I, the South of Thames races - In the South of Thames Junior we could win a set of team medals - the County, Area and National races. By and large the Walkers always do fully support the Club fixtures so lets make sure this year that the Cross-Country runners do so as well. Best wishes to all for a successful winter season. items.s: PRESIDENTIAL HONOURS Career summaries of Clive Shippen, newly elected President of Surrey AAA, and Bill Lucas D.F.C., newly elected President of the Southern Counties AAA. PRESIDENTIAL HONOURS The current year sees 2 of our officials achieving the highest honours that the Surrey and Southern AAA's can confer. Clive Shippen has been elected President of Surrey AAA's and Bill Lucas D.F.C. has been elected President of the Southern Counties AAA's. For our newer members we summarise briefly the athletic careers of these, our distinguished members. Clive Shippen Clive Shippen, who will be 50 in December, became Belgrave President in 1972 at about which period he resumed his athletics career. Vets running was really gaining popularity and his achievements reminded us of some of his runs as a younger man particularly when he won the Vets A.C. 1500m Champs. in 4.14.0 - on cinders. In 1973 and 1974 he helped Belgrave win the Veterans National C.C. Champs. He managed to combine running with official duties. He has served on the Surrey County Committee for over 20 years, was elected President of the South of the Thames C.C. Assoc. in 1977/78, is a member of the Southern Counties AAA's Committee and sits on their Championship and promotions sub-committee. He managed to Edit the Belgravian for much of this period - in his spare time! Clive's present project will take 6 years - he has been amassing as much as he can find on the Club's history and is planning to write and publish a 'Club History' for our Centenary year in 1987. (We will give more information next time). Bill Lucas DFC Bill Lucas D.F.C. joined Belgrave in 1936 and made an early impact by running in the second placed Belgrave team in the 1937 London - Brighton 12 stage relay. War saw Bill on active service in the R.A.F. where he progressed to Squadron Leader, and as a member of the elite Pathfinder Group was awarded the D.F.C. Resuming his athletic career he finished 3rd in the 1948 AAA's 3 Mile Champs. and was selected for the Olympic 5000m In 1949 he joined the Belgrave Committee and combined official duties with a successful athletics career. He served for many years as Cross Country and Road Hon. Sec. and was Surrey C.C. Team Manager in the 60's when Surrey won 2 Inter-Counties titles. Bill became Club President in 1963, Surrey President in 1970 and in this his retirement year it is most fitting that he should be honoured with the Presidency of the Southern Counties AAA's. items.sum: Tribute by Jack Goswell to Belgrave walker David King, fatally injured in a car accident while lying fourteenth in the London to Brighton Walk on 5 September 1981, tracing his walking career from joining the club in 1962 and his unique record in the London to Brighton.
items.s: A Tribute Tribute by Jack Goswell to Belgrave walker David King, fatally injured in a car accident while lying fourteenth in the London to Brighton Walk on 5 September 1981, tracing his walking career from joining the club in 1962 and his unique record in the London to Brighton. WALKING A Tribute With a strong team entered for the Annual London to Brighton Walk led by our President, Carl Lawton, Saturday September 5th 1981 was a day that all Belgravians looked forward to once again adding to our Clubs laurels with another victory in this old established Blue Ribbon event. "ALAS" out of victory came "TRAGEDY" to leave us all in the depths of despair at the finish, to learn the news of a serious car accident involving one of the 'Clubs Stalwarts' of the Brighton Road, 'David King' when lying fourteenth in the race, his injuries being so serious they proved fatal. What a tragedy to lose such a fine Belgravian three days before his thirty-ninth birthday. David lived at Bournemouth when he joined the Club on the 16th July 1962. His first walk in Belgrave colours was as an individual having to serve a fourteen months ban on his transfer from Bournemouth A.C. he finished 32nd in 50.52 in a field of 158 starters in the Chippenham to Calne six miles Walk, October 1962. Took part in his first Belgrave Open Walk in November of that year finishing 36th in 59.62, the start of a fine career in our walking teams. In December '62 he won his first Junior (under 21) 5 Miles Championship for the 'Olympic Cup' in 42.05. The following year he had improved to finish 12th in the Chippenham in 50.03 and won a Winning Team Medal in the Belgrave Open 7 of 1963 with 15th in 56.07. He very quickly lost his 'Junior Status' by leading a Winning Team home in the 'Garnet Cup' 10 Miles Championship in February 1964 being 5th in 83.56. This was the start of a momentous year, his first National R.W.A. 10 Miles fifth man home for the Club, then came his first Club 20 Miles Championship, finishing third in 2.56.48. From now on he had found his forte - distance events. After a first R.W.A. National 50Kms in July '64 at Enfield, when he was fourth scoring member of a Winning Team, 17th in 4.43.56 thereby obtaining his first R.W.A. National Medal, he won team medals. Four winning, two seconds and a third only missing this event five times since 1964. Next in only his third long distance all in August 1964 the Hastings to Brighton 38 miles he finished 2nd individual to our International Ray Middleton in 5.52.25, and the first of three Winning Team, and four Third Team medals he has won in this event, which he has competed in every year since. Eighteen in all up to August of this year, many times being "fourth" man home for the Club, and with only "three" to score, just missing scoring in Teams. This event led up to his marvellous record in the "Brighton" on September 5th 1964, his first one, he finished "Third" individual in 8.46.07 and gained a "second" Team Medal, going on to establish a unique record. Competing in every one since "Eighteen" in all, from 1964 - 1981. He only retired once in 1966, winning Team Medals 'eight' in all 'five' second Team Medals. Two years the club did not start, and one year did not finish a team. He won the "Brighton" Club Championship "three" times, second "six" times, "third" four times. What an ill turn of fate that he was not allowed to add to this marvellous record when only three odd miles from the finish of this years event. Although these were David's main events, he still carried our colours in other events up and down the country. What more can one say about this "True Belgravian" these words of mine do little to explain little of one of "Life's Tragedys" that he should be taken from us. What we do say is:- It was a privilege to have known him, and enjoyed his company for twenty years and convey the heartfelt sympathy of the whole Club to his wife and young family and parents at this terrible time. items.s: Walking Reports Carl Lawton's walking reports: a further tribute to Dave King, thanks for the Open 7 prize fund, a review of the summer's walking, then race-by-race reports and results from April to September 1981, including his course-record win in the Plymouth to Dawlish 42 miles, George Beecham becoming a Centurion, team wins in the Southern Track League, Hastings to Brighton and S.A. 20 km, Lawton's victory in the London to Brighton, marred by Dave King's death, and three races on 13 September. To write a few notes summing up the past few months successes and failures is sometimes easy, sometimes difficult. To have written it once and then to start again because of the tragic circumstances that occurred on the Brighton road is without doubt, distressing. Dave King was a team man, a Belgrave man, more you could not ask for. He could be relied upon to finish and in many cases bring home winning teams in longer distance events. The Hastings and London - Brighton roads were almost home to him, he had walked them so many times, but sadly no more. I for one will miss his humour, his enjoyment of life, his comradeship, his teamsmanship, but most of all I will miss a Belgravian. But back to the more mundane tasks, I regret in the previous issue I overlooked to thank those who helped out with the Open 7-Prize Fund last year, thus enabling me to once again give prizes far outweighing entry fees, and with no other form of sponsorship. Although I do not usually make particular mention I feel I must specially thank Bob Barnes for his efforts in raising over £50 towards the Fund. This year it is nearly Open 7 time again, and again I make the request for assistance in all forms, don't forget the date - November 28th. What of the summer? Fairly successful, with wins in the Track League, Southern 20 km, 50 kms Hastings and Brighton but no teams in the Leicester and no National placings were disappointments. Congratulations to two Belgravians, Joe Scamell, at a modest 58, collected 3rd place in the Essex 50 kms, 4th man for Belgrave in the National 50 kms and then proceeded to complete the Hastings, and then the Brighton to finish in under 10 hours. Also to George Beecham who in the Endeavour 24 hours at Brighton became the newest member of the Centurions and together with John Morris won the team award. So onto the winter, with the present form of Eric Hall and Joe Scamell team places could be at a premium. Paul Blagg, now recovered from injury having had to miss all the summer season, hopes to be back to form and with him and full team turn outs, anything is possible. VICTORY AND TRAGEDY SEPTEMBER 5th 1981 - SATURDAY - LONDON - BRIGHTON There are times when a triumph can be marred by a tragedy to such an extent that the triumph seems almost worthless. To compete and complete the accolade of long distance walking the London to Brighton is in itself an achievement. To go to the head of the field and win the race and to be acclaimed with the names of Whitlock, Baker, Thompson, Pamich, Middleton is something extra. To do this and then hear two hours later that one of your team has died as a result of injuries received on the very same road you had just passed along, is to say the least shattering. It could have been anyone, unfortunately it was Dave. He never won a Brighton, but he held a record, more winning Brighton team medals than anyone else, eight in all, this year would have been 9 had he finished, but he didn't and never will again. It is many years since Belgrave had 8 starters in the Brighton and all but Dave finished. John Hall completed his at the second attempt. Joe Scamell, well what can one say, his first attempt and under 10 hours and almost as fresh as a daisy at the finish. John Dunsford and Ron Day reliable as ever. A gem of a place, thatched cottages with a village green and adjacent clubhouse and the finish line just outside. The course was six laps with a big climb early in the lap - a heavy shower about halfway through the race refreshed the competitors and made the officials dash for cover. Chris Maddock (Dawlish & S.Devon) led the way with Carl isolated in second place. A few places later was John, unfortunately we had no third man so we had no interest in the team race. items.sum: Bill Laws's review of the young athletes' 1981 track season: Surrey, Southern Counties and junior international vests, a U.K. junior 4 x 1 mile record in the 100 x 1 mile relay, and two thirds in the Surrey 4 stage relays.
items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Bill Laws's review of the young athletes' 1981 track season: Surrey, Southern Counties and junior international vests, a U.K. junior 4 x 1 mile record in the 100 x 1 mile relay, and two thirds in the Surrey 4 stage relays. YOUNG ATHLETES With a few of our younger members entering their last year as track juniors everyone put in a good season's work with some very fine performances coming as a result. Almost all our youngsters set new p.b's and those that didn't tried hard - but now realise that injury or illness has no respect for individuals. It was great to see Mark Waller, Mark Sinclair and Pat Lyttle gain Surrey vests for the Junior Inter-Counties Champs, while John Gladwin and Stuart Paton won both S.C.A.A.A. vests and Junior International Honours. There were medals galore in the county, Borough Schools, London Schools and G.L.C. junior championships. In addition to this packed itinery all of our younger members turned out for the Senior Southern League track and field matches when called on and set a fine example of loyalty and support which made the life of the team manager(s) almost border on the enjoyable. (See T & F Section for details). Thank you everyone! Further honours came in the 100 x 1 mile relay (Ref.p. ) when a junior team consisting of Mark Sinclair, Paul Richley, Stuart Paton and John Gladwin broke the U.K. 4 x 1 mile record averaging 4:27 each. There is plenty of chance next year to better this by a wide margin looking at some of the season's later 1500m times. And finally at the start of the Road Running season our boys and youths gained two 3rds in the 4 Stage Surrey County Relay Champs. A really fine effort by everyone throughout the season. You have all put in a lot of hard work and will surely reap the benefits, both for yourselves as individuals and perhaps even more important for your team colleagues. Good luck through the winter and have a fine 1982 in Track and Field. Reports by ........ Championships, September 1981: John Gladwin and Stuart Paton retained titles and Pat Lyttle ran a 200m p.b. SEPTEMBER 5th 1981 - WEST LONDON - G.L.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS If Mark Sinclair had not been injured he would probably have won the GLC Junior Steeplechase as the winning time was well below his Inter-Counties result. However, it was not to be. Belgrave had good cause for celebration, however, with John Gladwin retaining his 800m title in 1.53.1 - while Stuart Paton retained his 1500m title with 1.56.3. The man to achieve the greatest satisfaction was Pat Lyttle who although only a first year Junior further lowered his 200m p.b. to 22.4 in finishing 4th. Pat has reduced his 100m time to 11.2 this year and has knocked a full 0.5 secs off his long sprint time. His coach reports that the big breakthrough should be next year. Stick with it Pat! Gladwin presses on John Gladwin tried valiently to recover from his early season injuries by stepping up his training schedules in a determined effort to make the U.K. Junior Team for the European Championships in August. Unfortunately, with Elliott and McGeorge finding top form in the 800m and only 2 to be sent for each event, things looked bleak for John. As things turned out the Junior AAA's Championships at Brighton Arena held on represented his last opportunity to gain selection. Such was the quality of competition that only the winners of each of the 5 heats could be sure of a place in the 800m final and John, of course, got the fastest heat. His winning time of 1.50.66 left him tired for the final which was only 2 hours later where he came 6th behind McGeorge and Elliott, but with another fast time of 1.51.80. Disappointed though he was at not making the U.K. team John plugged away. On August 7th he ran 1.51.02 in the AAA's 800m heats and after a short break got back on the winning trail, first retaining his Junior GLC 800m title with 1.53.1. A week later on 12th September he won the BMC 800m at Woodford in 1.51.3 and on the 19th September representing the Junior SCAAA against the North, Midlands and Wales he again won with a late burst after being boxed in - in the time of 1.53.6. So, at the end of it all, injuries had not enabled John to achieve his highest targets even though he had strung together the largest number of sub 1.54.0 runs in the Club's history (9 including the League meetings). Still only a second year T & F Junior next year we all hope that the winter will leave John free from injury and strong enough to really set the track alight!! items.s: YOUNGSTERS GAIN SURPRISE MEDALS Report of the Surrey Road Relay Championships at Brockwell Park, September 1981, where Belgrave's boys and youths each won bronze team medals, with colts', boys' and youths' results and a photograph of the squad. YOUNGSTERS GAIN SURPRISE MEDALS SEPTEMBER 12th 1981 - BROCKWELL PARK - SURREY ROAD RELAY CHAMPIONSHIPS With full teams in all age groups reflecting our growing band of young athletes we came away with 2 bronze medals. Particularly pleasing was the boys performance as the team medals were our first in this age group for at least two decades. Special mention for: Jim Biesty a new member who turned in one of the fastest colts times of the day. Andrew North who looked really sharp in moving the boys team from 8th to 3rd. Michael Blackmore who claimed to be unfit. Paul Richley who was within 3 seconds of Stu Paton's course record and Alister Horton who at the last minute ran to complete the Youth's team - his first run since being knocked off his bike in France by a speeding car. It was great to see the enthusiasm, and everyone giving 110% - particularly Alan Lammas who nailed 'A' team runner Carl Frater in the run-in. items.s: FAST TIME IN BELGRAVE '20' Report and results of the Belgrave Open 20 Mile Road Race of 18 July 1981, won by Norman Wilson (T.V.H.) in the third fastest time in its thirty-year history, with the Surrey title to Bob Roath and the Belgrave championship to Lionel Mann (two runners are printed as 4th in the Belgrave list). FAST TIME IN BELGRAVE '20' In near ideal conditions Norman Wilson (T.V.H.) won the Open 20 Mile Road Race on 18th July in the third fastest ever time of the thirty year history of the race - 1hr 41 min. 28 secs. He went into the lead very early on and was never challenged - had he been he could no doubt have got nearer to the course record of 1.39.47. With three in the first 5 team positions T.V.H. easily won the team race. Bob Roath of Walton won the Surrey Title with Ranelagh narrow winners of the Team Race. Lionel Mann took the Belgrave Title with Doug Maughan second and Tony Grant third. Twenty-three Belgravians finished the course - which is a record number. Sincere thanks to all those who helped with the race which, judging from outside comments, was a great success and much appreciated. Derek Crookes (Race Sec.) items.label: October 1981
items.sum: John Bicourt's first-hand account of the inaugural Berlin Marathon on 27 September 1981, won by Ian Ray, in which Bicourt finished 10th in 2.25.14 and won the 35-40 age group.
items.s: BICOURT IN BERLIN John Bicourt's first-hand account of the inaugural Berlin Marathon on 27 September 1981, won by Ian Ray, in which Bicourt finished 10th in 2.25.14 and won the 35-40 age group. BICOURT IN BERLIN SEPTEMBER 27th 1981 - BERLIN - MARATHON Berlin has now joined the many other major cities of the world in staging a mass marathon. It's inaugural event got under way on September 27th on a warm and sunny Sunday morning. 4,500 runners in all categories assembled in the park in front of the Reichstag. Helicopters clattered overhead, T.V. camera crews were busy taking in the scene and the expectant crowds lined the road away from the start. The maroon was fired at precisely 9.30 a.m. by guest of honour, Kee Ti Sohn of Korea, the '36 Olympic marathon victor, and we were off. There was a good number of British runners in the field, mainly because of the large British army contingent in the city, but also from the many who had come from England including a British marathon squad from the BAAB of five men and two ladies. Favourite on time had to be 2.11.50 performer, John Dimmock of the U.S.A. but my bet was for Ian Ray the best of the British group. For the first mile or two, the runners were settling down and similar level groups soon established themselves (once they had got by the wheelchair 'runners' .... one of whom had dangerously run his chair right into me and almost brought me down). I was aiming to run 2.20 pace and knew that I needed to be around 16.30 for the first 5k (too many runners - at all levels - completely blow it by going too fast in the early stages when they feel good, not fully realising the toll of the final 4 miles ... as I knew from my sorry experience in N.Y. last year where I took 40 minutes for the final six miles!!) 5k came up at 16.22 and I looked around to see who I was running along with. Five of us were about a hundred metres from the leaders and a similar distance in front of the next group. Two of the BAAAB squad and two other British lads plus me. Ray Maule (2. 18.) John Robertshaw (2.18) Bill Venus and John Barker, both p.b's in the low 2.20's - So I was in good company. The miles rolled by and the leaders only slowly drew away. Nobody was gaining. We went through 10k in 33.03, 20k in 66.42. After 25k the temperature really began to go up. At around 25k positions began to change; the going was getting hard. Robertshaw made an effort and moved away. From the leading group Paul Eales was caught along with a couple of others and two more runners had dropped out. I had no real idea of my position but thought I must be about 15th. Soon I was on my own. Barker and Venus just slipped behind. At 35k I knew I could finish but I was becoming stiff. Still on my own, and now gaining on some ahead I jogged on (and jogging was what it had become). It was very hot and sunny. The people lining the way were clapping and cheering. Rounding a bend, I found myself just a few yards down on Ray Maule and he offered no resistance as I went by. I managed to pass three more before the finish and also held off (by .8) a fast closing runner who as it turned out would have won my category, the 35-40 age group if he'd got by and got the 24c gold coin I got instead!! The finish was in the main shopping street. Shower cabins, stretcher beds, toilets, blankets, food and drink - all were beautifully organised to be available as you came in. Hoards of young students looked after everyone. Ian Ray as predicted won and undoubtedly his performance was worth a couple of minutes faster in cooler conditions. Twenty eight sub 2.20 runners took part and the highlights were transmitted nationally on T.V. That evening Ian Ray went live in a sports chat show and the general opinion in the press the next day was that of a huge success - but what marathon these days isn't. J. items.sum: Bill Laws's review of the 1981 track and field season: an improvised secretarial team, Irish Guards recruits, Derek Williams's injury, Mark Lindsey Bailey's support, Ernest Obeng's win over Allan Wells and 16th place in Sutton League Division 1.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Bill Laws's review of the 1981 track and field season: an improvised secretarial team, Irish Guards recruits, Derek Williams's injury, Mark Lindsey Bailey's support, Ernest Obeng's win over Allan Wells and 16th place in Sutton League Division 1. TRACK AND FIELD It has proved impossible to find any individual to take over the T & F Secretarial job and consequently a small team comprising Leo Coy, Colin Pearson and yours truly was cobbled together in an attempt to get the show on the road. Inevitably there were problems at the beginning of the season and it was not until June/July that we were able to get our communications sorted out with those of our members who are scattered around the U.K. In the meantime the coaching scheme (see separate report) had progressed well and had enabled us to attract a strong membership from the 1st Battalion Irish Guards stationed at Chelsea Barracks. Fortunately our new members were anxious for as much competition as possible prior to the Army Championships on July 28 (which they duly won) and on two occasions we turned out very strong teams which, if they could be reproduced regularly, would make a mark in the British League. However, the Majority of the Guards will be moving away next year and once again we shall be relying on our improving juniors who this year have transformed the middle distance and sprint results. Many of our more experienced members, particularly the field events specialists, have not been able to turn out this year. We will need them next year. On the individual side the progress of our younger members has been good (see Young Athletes Section). Derek Williams looked as though he was heading for a very good year after winning the Surrey Long Jump and coming second in the U.K. Championships, but injury struck yet again and he was sidelined for most of the season. As usual Mark Lindsey Bailey provided solid support in several events and travelled down from Edinburgh for most of our Sutton League matches. He was also very active for Edinburgh University. But of course pride of place must go to Ernest Obeng who has had his best ever season and strung together a series of high quality 100m's culminating in that now famous victory over Olympic 100m Champion Alan Wells in the Coca Cola Meeting on September 11th. And so at the end of a frenetic 5 months we look back with satisfaction on achieving 16th place out of 25 in the Sutton League Div.1. This was the same as last year, but at one point early season, we believed that such a result would be impossible to achieve. Reports by .......... items.s: Southern League: MAY 2nd 1981 - WINDSOR - MATCH 1 Report and Belgrave results from the first Southern League match at Windsor on 2 May 1981, where a weakened Belgrave team finished fifth of five. Southern League MAY 2nd 1981 - WINDSOR - MATCH 1: We travelled to Windsor knowing that this match could be our hardest. Windsor who had been relegated from the National League last year would dearly wish to show their superiority while the other 3 Clubs had all finished above us last season. As it turned out we were well and truly hammered due to the absence of several of our key men. Included among these were Ernest Obeng (Exams), Snowy Brooks ('fm), Ian Duncan (injury), Stuart Paton (representing SCAAA), Mark Lindsey Bailey and Paul Whitby (both moved North), John Aska, Dave Bailey, Kevin Clarke and several others. To compensate everyone gave 110% and there were several good performances. Pat Lyttle ran well to gain 3rd in the 100m. Derek Williams competed in six events. Mark Shippen made a welcome return to finish 2nd in the pole-vault and Tom Dowdall ran himself into the ground to set a p.b. 3000 s.c. Ex field events Captain John Martin travelled from Swindon to help out and in the open 1500m John Gladwin ran a 4.02.0 time trial to demonstrate that his leg injury had healed. Subsequently we calculated that with a full team we would have made 3rd. What would we do next time? items.s: MAY 30th 1981 - CRYSTAL PALACE - MATCH 2 Southern League match 2 at Crystal Palace on 30 May 1981, where a near-full Belgrave team missed first place by a single point behind Surrey A.C. MAY 30th 1981 - CRYSTAL PALACE - MATCH 2 After Match 1's disaster we wrote to everyone and it was with a sigh of relief that they arrived. Paul Whitby (temprarily in Cumbria) Mark LB (from Edinburgh), Ernest Obeng from Reading (or was it Rome?), Snowy Brooks (Heathfarm) John Asta (emigrated to Birmingham), Reg Hopkins Jnr. (from his new shop), - and so on. And they did us proud, we missed first place by just a single point - and we would have had a clear lead if we had realised it was a double meet with a 1 p.m. start! The times below show the results. The enthusiastic support had to be felt to be believed and the final relays almost gave us victory. The 4 x 100 squad set a seasons best and in the 4 x 400 in which we were last after the first leg. John Gladwin was timed at 49.4 with Stu Paton, looking diminutive against some large 400m men, ran a remarkable 50.4. JUNE 6th 1981 - WEST LONDON - MATCH 3 After 2 matches we had climbed to 17th place in the League. This meeting brought us down with a jolt, for again we were last. The main factor was a management error. Tragically we thought this was a single meet, but as luck would have it the match was well under way when our team arrived. We cannot print the detailed results as host team Havering never returned them to the Division I Secretary. Perhaps thats a blessing in disguise. It could easily have been so different. JUNE 27th 1981 - HANDYCROSS - MATCH 4 Our new influx of members contributed to our first win of the season and filled current weakspots particularly in some of the field events. Highlight of the meet was Ernest's 200m victory, not because of the time, but because of the snazzy orange long-johns which he sported to keep out a cold north wind. Derek Williams competing in fewer events than usual (and due to the good support), took the opportunity to compete all jumps, ironically his 6th long jump, taken even though he was a clear winner, resulted in an injury which was to put him out for the rest of the season. Mark Shippen missed the coach and competed in the Southern Counties Champs. items.s: JULY 25th 1981 - COPTHALL - MATCH 5 Southern League match 5 at Copthall on 25 July 1981, a second Belgrave win that lifted the club to 12th, with Steve Sampson's pole vault p.b. and John Bicourt back to fitness. JULY 25th 1981 - COPTHALL - MATCH 5 Our last win brought us up to 16th in the League and everyone turned out for this one. Our new members from the Irish Guards were eager to get a final work out before the Army Champs. And so we saw some first class performances. Particularly impressive was Steve Sampson's continued improvement with a massive p.b. improvement in the P.V. If only this man would train and take his talent seriously! It was good to see John Bicourt return to fitness and of course the youngsters once again did us proud. The pole vault took all afternoon and most of the team stayed late to watch our lads clinch another fine win which moved us to 12th in the League with one match to go. AUGUST 15th 1981 - NEW RIVER - MATCH 6 August is always a difficult month due to holidays. On this occasion our army based members were all on leave with the exception of Alan Benn who ran his first 5000m. Ernest again turned out and we missed first place by just points. We did not receive official results and the following is all we could retrieve from Colin Pearson's notes. Our 3rd place was sufficient to give us a final 10th place in the League. If you look back at all the near misses it will be apparent that we could well have finished in the top three. Indeed several of the teams above us had been handed defeats by our teams during the season. Well done everyone!! items.sum: Belgrave, helped by their Irish Guards members, finished 5th of 8 in the Kinnaird Trophy open meeting at West London Stadium on 18 July 1981, won by Shaftesbury.
items.s: JULY 18th 1981 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - KINNAIRD TROPHY: Belgrave, helped by their Irish Guards members, finished 5th of 8 in the Kinnaird Trophy open meeting at West London Stadium on 18 July 1981, won by Shaftesbury. JULY 18th 1981 - WEST LONDON STADIUM - KINNAIRD TROPHY: Poly's famous Kinnaird Trophy was on offer for this Open meeting organised jointly by TVH and Poly. We expected to be out-classed by the 5 National League Clubs especially, as Derek Williams was injured, Ernest Obeng was on his overseas Tour and 2 of our Juniors were competing in a Home Counties International at Meadowbank while 3 other Juniors were running for Surrey in the Junior Inter-Counties at Brighton. However, ably supported by our Irish Guards members we performed very well with Mike Scott, Tony Nwosu, Steve Samson, Jim Dunn and Phil Mckay among those achieving p.b.'s. In the final count we finished a creditable 5th out of 8 beating National Division side Enfield.
